narration: The pipeline has two stages. The Initializing Process, on the left, prepares a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting model for watermarking.
It starts from the pre-trained 3D-GS model G-o. Its parameters are frozen, shown by the closed padlock in the corner.
That model is passed into Frequency Guided Densification, or FGD, the module that decides where Gaussians should be removed and where they should be added.
FGD runs in two phases. Phase 1 removes 3D Gaussians: each Gaussian is scored by its contribution to rendering quality, and the low-contribution ones, outlined with dashes, are pruned.
Phase 2 splits Gaussians in high frequency areas. Rendered views of the scene are first patchified into a regular grid of image patches.
Each patch is sent through a Discrete Fourier Transform, producing the frequency magnitude maps shown on the right.
High frequency content is detected by taking the Hadamard product of the transformed patch P-tilde with a quadratic mask Q that suppresses the low frequency centre.
The patches with the strongest high frequency response are selected, and the 3D Gaussians covering those regions are split into finer ones.
The result is the densified model, After FGD 3D-GS G-o-prime, still frozen but now with extra Gaussians concentrated in high frequency areas.
FGD also yields a gradient mask over the Gaussian attributes: mean, colour, scale, rotation and opacity. It marks which parameters are allowed to change.
During fine-tuning the mask is applied as a Hadamard product with the optimizer updates, so only the selected attributes of the unfrozen model are modified.
This produces the fine-tuned watermarked model, 3D-GS G-w. Its padlock is open, marking it as the trainable model.
The watermarked model is rendered into an image of the scene, shown by the red rendering arrow.
The rendered image goes through a Discrete Wavelet Transform, which separates it into a low frequency band and several high frequency sub-bands.
The high frequency sub-bands are where the message is embedded, so they are compared against the high frequency bands of the ground truth.
The low frequency band is fed to the pre-trained, frozen decoder, which recovers the decoded message.
Three losses supervise training. The reconstruction and LPIPS losses keep the rendered image close to the ground truth.
The wavelet loss L-w aligns the high frequency bands of the render with those of the ground truth.
The message loss L-m compares the decoded message with the fixed message that was supposed to be hidden.
All three are summed into L-total, which drives the optimizer. Its gradients, filtered by the gradient mask, update the watermarked 3D Gaussians, closing the loop.
